verdict.rationale: Mercury's own REST API exposes accounting-relevant data. Developers can list and get transactions, update transaction metadata, upload attachments, create, edit and delete categories, download statements, list merchants, and manage customers and invoices through the Accounts Receivable API, with read-write scoped tokens. However, there is no dedicated accounting API: QuickBooks/Xero/NetSuite sync is a product integration, not documented as API-manageable. missing for 10: a dedicated accounting/ledger API (chart of accounts, journal entries, GL mappings), API control over accounting-software sync, a publicly downloadable OpenAPI spec, independent hands-on corroboration of the accounting endpoints.

support.subject: As a developer, I can view and manage accounting data through a dedicated API

citations.quote: List all transactions, Get a transaction by ID, Update transaction metadata, Upload a transaction attachment; Categories: List/Create/Edit/Delete a category; Statements: Download account statement PDF
Accounts Receivable API: Customers (List/Create/Get/Update/Delete a customer); Invoices (List/Create/Get/Update/Cancel an invoice, Download invoice PDF)
Write actions such as making payments, categorizing transactions, creating invoices, and uploading receipts
There are three types of tokens: read-only, read-write, and custom.
